'''Antonio Helio de Castro Neto''', often referred to as the '[https://www.nanotechnologyworld.org/post/meet-the-godfather-of-graphene Godfather of Graphene,'] is a Brazilian-born [[physicist]] who serves as the founder and director of the [[Centre for Advanced 2D Materials]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://graphene.nus.edu.sg/team_member/antonio-castro-neto/|title=Antonio Castro Neto &#124;}}</ref> (previously known as the Graphene Research Centre<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://graphene.nus.edu.sg/about-us/|title=ABOUT US &#124;}}</ref>) and as Co-Director of the [https://ifim.nus.edu.sg/people/antonio-helio-castro-neto/ Institute for Functional Intelligent Materials (IFIM)] at the [[National University of Singapore]]. He is a condensed matter theorist known for his work in the theory of [[metals]], [[magnets]], [[superconductors]], [[graphene]] and [[two-dimensional materials]]. He is a distinguished professor in the Departments of Materials Science Engineering,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.eng.nus.edu.sg/mse/staff/castro-neto-antonio-helio/ | title=NUS Engineering &#124; Home }}</ref> and Physics<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physics.nus.edu.sg/staff/antonio.html|title=Department of Physics|website=www.physics.nus.edu.sg}}</ref> and a professor at the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering.<ref name="auto">https://www.eng.nus.edu.sg/ece/staff/castro-neto-antonio-helio/</ref> He was elected as a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2003.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/units/dcmp/fellowship/index.cfm|title=APS Fellowship|website=www.aps.org}}</ref> In 2011 he was elected as a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/sites/default/files/AR_2012_AAAS-fellows.pdf |title=AAAS Fellows|website=aaas.org|access-date=28 August 2023}}</ref>

== Education ==
In 1984, Castro Neto attended the State University of Campinas [[University of Campinas|(UNICAMP)]].{{Citation needed|date=February 2020}} In Campinas, he completed his undergraduate and [[Master of Science]] degree in physics under Amir O. Caldeira. In 1991, he moved to the [[United States]] where he obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] under the supervision of [[Eduardo Fradkin]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite journal |title=Bosonization of Fermi liquids|first1=A. H. Castro|last1=Neto|first2=Eduardo|last2=Fradkin|date=April 15, 1994|journal=Physical Review B|volume=49|issue=16|pages=10877–10892 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.49.10877 |pmid=10009931|arxiv=cond-mat/9307005|bibcode=1994PhRvB..4910877C|s2cid=14320891}}</ref><ref name="auto2"/> His PhD thesis dealt with the understanding and description of the lowest energy excitations of [[Fermi liquid theory|Fermi liquids]].<ref name="auto1"/>

== Career ==
After graduation in 1994, he joined the Institute for Theoretical Physics (currently, [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]]) at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Physics |url=https://www.bu.edu/physics/ |access-date=2025-10-14 |website=www.bu.edu}}</ref> There he studied the electronic properties of nanomaterials and [[nanostructure]]s under Matthew Fisher. In 1995, he moved to the [[University of California, Riverside]] as an assistant professor. In 2000, he moved to [[Boston University]] as a professor of physics.

Castro Neto published on theoretical aspects of graphene such as the effect of vacancies in the electronic properties;<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Disorder Induced Localized States in Graphene|first1=Vitor M.|last1=Pereira|first2=F.|last2=Guinea|first3=J. Castro Neto |url=https://scholar.google.com.br/citations?user=4kNDbNEAAAAJ&hl=pt-BR |access-date=2023-02-26 |website=scholar.google.com.br}}</ref>

In 2008, he moved to the National University of Singapore, starting the Graphene Research Centre (GRC) in 2010<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nanowerk.com/news/newsid=25564.php|title=National University of Singapore's Graphene Research Centre opens S$15 million graphene fabrication facility|website=Nanowerk}}</ref> with facilities for the synthesis, characterization, and device fabrication of graphene devices.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://physicsworld.com/a/solar-sandwich-could-cover-a-variety-of-surfaces/|title=Solar 'sandwich' could cover a variety of surfaces|date=May 13, 2013|website=Physics World}}</ref> In 2014, the GRC was expanded by a grant of the National Research Foundation of Singapore to explore other 2D materials beyond graphene and their heterostructures<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://phys.org/news/2016-07-two-dimensional-materials-revolutionary-graphene.html|title=Two-dimensional materials 'as revolutionary as graphene'|website=phys.org}}</ref> with the creation of the Centre for Advanced 2D Materials.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/ntu-nus-push-materials-science-frontiers|title=NTU, NUS push materials science frontiers|date=December 16, 2016|website=The Straits Times}}</ref>

Castro Neto has initiated and later closed 3 science spinoffs out of the [[National University of Singapore|National University in Singapore]]: 2D Materials in 2015;<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detailed Startup Profile |url=https://www.asiaclimatehub.com/startup-databases?startupName=2DM&logo=https%253A%252F%252Fv5.airtableusercontent.com%252Fv3%252Fu%252F38%252F38%252F1739527200000%252FJG1bmc4AfbxnIxQqDccanw%252Fj0ZCdq1IuyKnJlld6olcR3kAqcdmBCoTFTUFmrHyJSMj27JGZFFJ6icpar8oybnyglwNBvjVmjhI6Dst_TdX2loaRmYNelwO5aUTnb3ZsGubC8lR1BMroHAiuHlL5gG4h-DgIvA7Bl5L3Vv_T-BTKA%252FAfpFDvySOC84q3AOUULkDAEdkKoHFK1OWvsWFZaZ_h4&website=http%253A%252F%252Fwww.2dmsolutions.com%252F&linkedIn=https%253A%252F%252Fwww.linkedin.com%252Fcompany%252F2dmsolutions%252F&oneliner=Manufacturer%2520of%2520high%2520performance%2520graphene%2520as%2520an%2520industrial%2520additive%2520to%2520enhance%2520the%2520properties%2520of%2520many%2520industrial%2520materials.&other_investors=%2520-%2520&founded=2015&funding=5.13&category=Industry&subcategory=Construction&country=Singapore&fundingStage=Seed&productStage=Pilot&totalRaised=5.13 |access-date=2025-04-21 |website=www.asiaclimatehub.com |language=en}}</ref> MADE Advanced Materials in 2017<ref>{{Cite web |last=CDTM |title=Center for Digital Technology and Management |url=https://cdtm.com/startups/made-advanced-materials |access-date=2025-04-21 |website=CDTM |language=en}}</ref> and Graphene Watts in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Castro Neto, Antonio Helio – Electrical and Computer Engineering |url=https://cde.nus.edu.sg/ece/staff/castro-neto-antonio-helio/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250130143836/https://cde.nus.edu.sg/ece/staff/castro-neto-antonio-helio/ |archive-date=2025-01-30 |access-date=2025-04-21 |website=cde.nus.edu.sg |language=en-US}}</ref>
